What is the atomic number of Germanium?
Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
In what year did Steve Jobs die?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year was Tardigrade discovered?
Tardigrade: The earliest known fossil is from the Cambrian, some 500 million years ago.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.
NASA X-43: Boeing. The NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Who is credited with discovering Phoenix?
Phoenix (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Named after the mythical phoenix, it was first depicted on a celestial atlas by Johann Bayer in his 1603 Uranometria.
Who is credited with discovering Glycerol?
Glycerol: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Who is credited with discovering Theory of relativity?
Theory of relativity: Albert Einstein. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.
Who is credited with discovering Sombrero Galaxy?
Sombrero Galaxy: Pierre Méchain. It is a member of the Virgo II Groups, a series of galaxies and galaxy clusters strung out from the southern edge of the Virgo Supercluster.

Produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex, this mineralocorticoid is the body's key sodium-saver, quietly governing blood pressure and potassium balance in the kidney — which hormone is it?
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.
This psychological term describes a diverse set of deficits in the ability to feel or anticipate pleasure, and is recognized as a diagnostic feature in the DSM-5 — what's the term?
Anhedonia is a diverse array of deficits in hedonic function, including reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure.
Four novels and fifty-six short stories about a certain consulting detective made his name — but this knighted British writer-physician also invented Professor Challenger. Who was he?
Arthur Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 - 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
Native to Europe, this small white-petaled, yellow-centered lawn flower is called 'common,' 'lawn,' or 'English' in various regions — what is its scientific name?
Bellis perennis (p-), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.
This rigid, mineralized organ of the vertebrate skeleton produces both red and white blood cells and helps regulate the body's acid-base balance — what is it?
Bone is a rigid organ that constitutes part of the skeleton in most vertebrate animals.

What suborder of orthopteran insects — its Latin name meaning 'chisel-bearing,' after the stout shape of its members' egg-laying organs — includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera are a suborder of orthopteran insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
Mature females are cows, the intact males are bulls, and the castrated males pull plows as oxen — all names for one widespread domesticated bovine kept as livestock. What animal is it?
Cattle (Bos taurus) are large, domesticated, bovid ungulates widely kept as livestock.
This roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle, generated within an organism but tuned by cues like daylight, is regulated by an internal biological clock — what is it called?
Circadian rhythm is a natural oscillation that repeats roughly every 24 hours.
Lending its metal to sterling silver, cupronickel coins, and strain-gauge alloys, this element carries atomic number 29 and a name drawn from the Latin 'cuprum' — what is it?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.

This American nuclear physicist worked on the Manhattan Project and later led the Federation of American Scientists, best remembered for his 1959 testimony that helped sink a controversial cabinet nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill (November 11, 1919 - December 14, 2008) was an American nuclear physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II and was head of the Federation of American Scientists.
This scarab superfamily insect is famous for rolling balls of animal droppings, a behavior the Ancient Egyptians linked to the god Khepri — which creature is it?
Dung beetle are beetles that feed on feces.

This broad set of measures — taken by individuals, advocacy groups, and governments alike — aims to prevent pollution, conserve natural resources, and maintain ecological balance, sometimes repairing existing damage — what is it called?
Environmental protection refers to the taking of measures to protecting the natural environment, prevent pollution and maintain ecological balance.
A Swiss linguist and philosopher who died in 1913, this thinker's ideas shaped 20th-century linguistics, psychoanalysis, and anthropology alike, according to one of his translators — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure (26 November 1857 - 22 February 1913) was a Swiss linguist, semiotician and philosopher.

Discovered in Paris in 1875 and bearing the symbol Ga on the periodic table, this soft, silvery chemical element has such a low melting point — just below 30°C — that it turns liquid at warm room temperature. Name this element?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

Five species of this group of plants — rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane — together cover 46 percent of the world's arable land, alongside two related families, sedges and rushes. What kind of plant is this?
Grass refers to various families of plants.
Which 19th-century American economist's wildly popular treatise Progress and Poverty argued that a single tax on the value of land could build a more just and productive society?
Henry George (September 2, 1839 - October 29, 1897) was an American political economist, social philosopher and journalist.

In this heart condition, muscle tissue — most often in the wall between the ventricles — thickens for no obvious reason, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes its electrical rhythm — name the condition?
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.

This Russian and Soviet physiologist discovered classical conditioning through famous experiments involving dogs, and won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his separate research into digestion — who is he?
Holding doctorates in both anthropology and medicine, this SS physician earned the grim nickname 'Angel of Death' for his experiments and selections at Auschwitz — who was he?

Josef Mengele (16 March 1911 - 7 February 1979), often dubbed the "Angel of Death", was a German military officer and physician during World War II at the Soviet front and then at Auschwitz during the Holocaust.
This inflammation of the voice box causes symptoms ranging from a hoarse voice to complete voice loss, usually clearing up within two weeks. Name the condition?
Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx (voice box). The primary symptom is loss of some vocal function, ranging from hoarse voice to no voice at all.
Used since pre-Columbian times as a pack animal that can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles, which domesticated South American camelid has wool low in lanolin?
Llama (Spanish) (Lama glama) is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era.
Though it's the strongest bone in the face, this lower jawbone tends to deform with age and is prone to fractures — what is it called?

Mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower - and typically more mobile - component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).
Aristotle called this the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes the most fundamental structure of reality, from existence itself to the categories of being — what is it?
Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that examines the basic nature or most fundamental structure of reality.
Their name means "little fly" in Spanish, and biologists class them as micropredators — all sip flower nectar, but the females of many species also drink blood. What are they?
Mosquito are a family of small flies consisting of 3,600 species.

This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not the Earth, at the center of the universe in a 1543 book published just before his death — likely arriving independently at an idea Aristarchus of Samos had floated eighteen centuries earlier. Who is he?
Nicolaus Copernicus (19 February 1473 - 24 May 1543) was a Renaissance polymath who formulated a model of the universe that placed the Sun rather than Earth at its center.
Many species in this cosmopolitan, often-fragrant family live as epiphytes on trees, and some have ditched leaves entirely — relying on highly specialized pollination tricks instead. What are they?
Orchid are plants that belong to the family Orchidaceae, a diverse and widespread group of flowering plants with blooms that are often colourful and fragrant.
This pulse crop, given the scientific name Pisum sativum by Linnaeus in 1753, is usually eaten as a vegetable via its small round seeds. What is it?
Pea is a pulse or fodder crop, but the word often refers to the seed or sometimes the pod of this flowering plant species.

A pnictogen with only one stable isotope and atomic number 15, this element hides in Earth's crust mostly as phosphate rock and readily builds a vast family of organic and inorganic compounds. Which element is it?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Part of the critical theory framework and closely tied to critical race theory, this field analyzes history, literature, and discourse shaped by imperial power — what field is it?

Postcolonialism is the academic study of the cultural, political and economic consequences of colonialism and imperialism, focusing on the impact of human control and exploitation of colonized people and their lands.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes includes some of the world's largest and kills by coiling to suffocate rather than by injecting venom — what is the family called?

Pythonidae are a family of nonvenomous snakes found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
With a surface temperature over 12,000 Kelvin and a radius more than seventy times the Sun's, this blue supergiant is the brightest point of light in Orion — which star?
Rigel is a blue supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion.
This systematic discipline builds testable explanations about nature and society, and is continuously challenged and validated by the community that practices it. What is it?
Science is a systematic discipline that builds and organises knowledge in the form of testable explanations about nature and society.
The brightest star in the night sky, this star sits in the constellation Canis Major and is actually a binary system paired with a faint white dwarf companion — name the star?
Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, located in the southern constellation of Canis Major.

Held together by its own gravity, this luminous sphere of plasma is the type of object our Sun is, with roughly 4,000 of them visible to the naked eye on a clear night - what are these objects called?
Star is a luminous spheroid of plasma held together by self-gravity.
This genus of flowering plants in the daisy family is better known by the fluffy-seeded lawn weed it produces, with two European species now invasive nearly worldwide. What is it?
Taraxacum is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae which consists of species commonly known as dandelions.
This family of large, long-legged flies can be identified by a maxillary-palp segment longer than the other three combined, and typically has thirteen segments in each antenna. Name the family?
Tipulidae is a family of large crane flies in the order Diptera.
A physician before politics, this German served as Angela Merkel's defence minister and in 2019 became President of the European Commission — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen (ne Albrecht; born 8 October 1958) is a German politician and physician who has served as President of the European Commission since 2019.
The first person to ever call himself a psychologist, this German founder of modern psychology launched Philosophische Studien, the field's first academic research journal — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt (16 August 1832 - 31 August 1920) was a German physiologist, philosopher, professor, and one of the fathers of modern psychology.

Best known for the Cities of Salt quintet chronicling how oil discovery upended traditional Bedouin life, this novelist's criticism of Middle Eastern elites led Saudi Arabia to revoke his citizenship — who is he?

Originally launched in 2008 as Bombardier's CSeries, this five-abreast narrow-body airliner family was rebranded in 2018 after a European aerospace giant acquired a majority stake. What's it called today?
Airbus A220: Canadian narrow-body airliner family. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
This three-star system includes Proxima, the closest star to the Sun, and shines as the third-brightest point in the night sky after Sirius and Canopus — which system?
Alpha Centauri: Star system in the Centaurus constellation.
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Also nicknamed the cross spider or diadem spider for the white markings on its back, this orb-weaver is native to Europe but was introduced to North America — what species is it?

Araneus diadematus: Species of spider. The spider species Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Named for the physicist who shared a 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie, this SI unit measures one radioactive decay event per second — which unit?
Becquerel: SI derived unit of radioactivity.
Despite its name, only the soles of this tawny, spotted feline's paws are actually dark — and at just 35 to 52 centimetres long, it ranks as Africa's smallest wild feline species — what animal is it?
Black-footed cat: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa.
Also known as warble flies or gadflies, the larvae of which insect family live as internal parasites in mammal flesh or gut, with one species routinely infesting humans?
Botfly: Parasitic insect. Dermatobia hominis is the only species of botfly known to parasitize humans routinely, though other species of flies cause myiasis in humans.
He piloted the Lunar Module Eagle in 1969 to become the second person to walk on the Moon, and after Jim Lovell's death in 2025 became the oldest living astronaut — who is he?
These biomolecules often follow the tidy empirical formula (CH2O)n, and as polysaccharides like starch, glycogen, and cellulose they store energy and build structure — what family are they?
Carbohydrate: Organic compound that consists only of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Consisting mainly of the brain and spinal cord — and, surprisingly, the retina too — this part of the body integrates information to coordinate an animal's activity — what is it?
Central nervous system: Brain and spinal cord. The rest of this article exclusively discusses the vertebrate central nervous system, which is radically distinct from all other animals.
Patented in 1948, this first-generation antihistamine blocks the H1 receptor to relieve allergy symptoms like hay fever within about two hours — what is it?
Chlorphenamine: Antihistamine used to treat allergies.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758 and introduced to North America to control aphids, this red beetle with seven black spots gets its genus name from the Latin word for 'scarlet' — which species?
Coccinella septempunctata: Species of beetle. It inhabits many regions with a temperate climate.
This mathematical framework assigns one or more numbers to each point in space so its exact position can be pinned down — the foundation of analytic geometry. What is it called?
Coordinate system: Method for specifying point positions.

Named from the Greek for "dark blue," this compound's signature group is a carbon atom triple-bonded to nitrogen — and its soluble salts, like the potassium and sodium versions, are infamously deadly. What is it?
Cyanide: Any molecule with a cyano group (C≡N)
Working alongside longtime colleague Ken Thompson, this American computer scientist co-created the Unix operating system and the C programming language — who is he?
Dennis Ritchie: American computer scientist known for Unix (1941–2011)
Nicknamed 'Spad' after a World War I fighter, this piston-engine attack plane flew from 1946 into the 1980s, an anachronism deep into the Jet Age — which aircraft?
Douglas A-1 Skyraider: American single engine attack aircraft.
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Historically used in the 18th century to track down escaped slaves, this large Brazilian dog breed of mastiff type now also serves as a guard dog and companion — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro: Brazilian breed of dog. The Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfilɐ bɾaziˈlejɾu]) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Coated in cornmeal and pan-cooked while still unripe, this dish was originally a Northeastern and Midwestern staple before a hit movie rebranded it as quintessentially Southern comfort food — what is it?
Fried green tomatoes: American dish. Fried green tomatoes is a culinary dish usually found in the United States, made from unripe (green) tomatoes coated with cornmeal and fried.

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)

This German engineer invented the high-speed petroleum engine, working alongside his lifelong partner Wilhelm Maybach to build small, fast motors they hoped to mount on any kind of vehicle. Who was he?
Gottlieb Daimler: German engineer, industrialist and automotive pioneer (1834–1900)
Often translated as 'Jewish law' but literally meaning 'the way of walking,' this body of religious rules draws on the Torah, the Talmud, and codes like the Shulchan Aruch — what is it called?
Halakha: Jewish rabbinical law. Halakha is often translated as "Jewish law", although a more literal translation might be "the way one proceeds" or "the way of walking".
With over 800 species lugging borrowed snail shells to shield their soft, non-calcified abdomens, this crustacean is essentially homeless without a hand-me-down home. What is it?
Stretching about a meter from crown to tail-tip, this deep-blue South American parrot is the largest of its kind and can be mistaken for a smaller relative — which vulnerable parrot?
Powered by four underperforming Lyulka turbojets, this aircraft became the first Soviet jet bomber to fly before being cancelled in September 1947 — which plane?
Ilyushin Il-22: 1947 Soviet bomber aircraft prototype. The Ilyushin Il-22, USAF/DOD designation Type 10, was the first Soviet jet-engined bomber to fly.
An Indian polymath and pioneer of radio microwave optics, he's also considered the father of Bengali science fiction — and even has a crater on the Moon named for him. Who was he?
Jagadish Chandra Bose: Physicist, biologist and botanist (1857–1937)
He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987, then later urged people to uninstall the product bearing his name and twice ran for U.S. president — who was he?
John McAfee: British and American programmer and businessman (1945–2021)

With oversized heads, dagger-like bills, and stubby tails, these 118 brightly colored bird species swoop from perches to nab prey — and despite reputation, many don't even live near water — what family of birds?
Kingfisher: Family of birds. The family contains 118 species and is divided into three subfamilies and 19 genera.
This small Arctic rodent is the unwitting star of a persistent myth that it hurls itself off cliffs in mass suicide — what is it?
Lemming: Tribe of rodents of the family Cricetidae.

Three of this crustacean's five pairs of legs bear claws, with the first pair often dramatically oversized, and its burrow-dwelling relatives include the Norway variety known as langoustine - which creature?
Lobster: Family of clawed marine crustaceans.
A field of artificial intelligence built on statistics and optimization, it develops algorithms that learn from data and handle unseen examples without being explicitly programmed — what is it?
Machine learning: Subset of artificial intelligence. Statistics and mathematical optimisation methods compose the foundations of machine learning.
On April 3, 1973, this Motorola engineer made history's first public call from a handheld cell phone on a Manhattan sidewalk — who is he?

Diagnosed when a person has at least three of five red flags -- including abdominal obesity and high blood pressure -- this cluster of conditions raises the risk of heart disease and diabetes in about a quarter of US adults. What is it?
Metabolic syndrome: Cluster of diseases occurring with obesity.

Prized for their fur and related to weasels and otters, these semiaquatic carnivores have established wild populations in Britain and Denmark after farm escapes and animal-rights releases — what are they?
Mink: Mammal in the family Mustelidae.
In this autoimmune disease the immune system attacks myelin, the insulation around nerve cells, so the central nervous system can't transmit signals properly — what condition?
Multiple sclerosis: Disease that damages the myelin sheaths around nerves.
Commonly called horsehair worms, these parasitoid animals get their nickname from the Gordian knot because of how they tangle themselves up — what phylum is this?

Nematomorpha: Phylum of parasitoid animals; horsehair worms. The adult worms are free-living, but the larvae are parasitic on arthropods, such as beetles, cockroaches, mantises, orthopterans, and crustaceans.
This Turkish-born American economist, a Harvard-trained NYU professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who foresaw the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis. Who is he?
With atomic number 76 and symbol Os, this bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and was once prized for fountain-pen nib tips — what is it?
Osmium: Chemical element with atomic number 76 (Os). Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

First described by a 17th-century French mathematician in 1653, this fluid mechanics principle states that a pressure change at any point in a confined, incompressible fluid is felt equally throughout it — what's it called?
Pascal's law: Principle in fluid mechanics. The law was established by French mathematician Blaise Pascal in 1653 and published in 1663.
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.

Often stereotyped as ferocious predators, these South American freshwater fish actually have varied diets that include plant matter, making them more omnivorous than their reputation suggests. What fish are they?
Piranha: Common name for certain fishes of the family Serrasalmidae.
Chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese all fall under this term for birds domesticated for meat, eggs, or feathers — what is it called?
Poultry: Domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, meat or feathers.
Forming the front-most part of the hip bone in vertebrates, this structure is made up of a superior ramus, an inferior ramus, and a body — which bone?
Pubis: Most forward-facing of the three main regions making up the os coxa.
Roughly 12 centimeters long in adults, this final section of the large intestine temporarily stores waste before it passes into the anal canal — what is it?
Rectum: Final portion of the large intestine. The rectum (pl.: rectums or recta) is the final straight portion of the large intestine in humans and some other mammals, and the gut in others.
Having spent years building theremins, this engineer debuted the first commercial synthesizer in 1964 and later the portable Minimoog — earning a spot in the Inventors Hall of Fame. Who is it?
Robert Moog: American electronic music pioneer (1934–2005)

The largest living reptile, whose males can top 1,000 kg and stretch six metres, ranges from India's coast through Southeast Asia to northern Australia — and earns its 'dangerous to humans' reputation. Which croc is it?
Saltwater crocodile: Species of reptile. It has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 1996.
Ejaculated through the urethra and containing fructose plus enzymes that help sperm survive their journey to fertilize an egg, this bodily fluid is also collected for animal breeding. What is it?
Semen: Reproductive biofluid of male or hermaphroditic animals.

A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep non-REM sleep occur in different brain regions at once, this condition can produce anything from bathroom trips to attempts at cooking or even driving — what is it?
Sleepwalking: Sleeping phenomenon combined with wakefulness.

Synthesized by Aristotle and taken as fact for two millennia, this superseded theory held that maggots could arise straight from dead flesh, until Louis Pasteur helped discredit it — what was it called?
Spontaneous generation: Theory of life arising from non-living matter.
Born from Russia's PAK FA programme begun in 1999 and carrying the internal name T-50, this twin-engine jet was the first Russian military aircraft built with stealth technology — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russian stealth multirole fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the brown raptor, this nocturnal bird of prey nests in tree hollows across Europe and is so territorial that evicted youngsters may starve — what is it?
Tawny owl: Stocky medium-sized owl species.

Marked by platelet counts that fall too low — sometimes below 50,000 per microliter and requiring emergency care — this blood disorder is the most common coagulation problem in ICU patients — what is it called?
Thrombocytopenia: Abnormally low levels of platelets in the blood.
This spiral-shaped bacterium, spread mainly through sexual contact and known only to infect humans and baboons, causes syphilis along with yaws and bejel — what is it?
Treponema pallidum: Species of bacterium. T. pallidum can enter the host through mucosal membranes or open lesions in the skin and is primarily spread through sexual contact.
Known as the Great Bear, this constellation contains the seven-star pattern nicknamed the Big Dipper — what's it called?
Ursa Major: Constellation in the northern sky.
Sporting prominent tusks and whiskers, this Arctic pinniped's Pacific males can weigh over 2,000 kilograms, making it second in size among pinnipeds only to the elephant seals — what animal?
Walrus: Species of marine mammal with tusks.
Named for the Aztec god of fire and lightning, this ancient Mexican dog breed comes in hairless and fully-coated varieties within the same litter — which breed?
Xoloitzcuintle: Hairless dog breed from Mexico.
What is the chemical symbol for thallium?
The symbol for thallium is Tl. Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.

Lance Reddick: Lance Solomon Reddick (June 7, 1962 – March 17, 2023) was an American actor.

Farrah Fawcett: Mary Ferrah Leni "Farrah" Fawcett (February 2, 1947 – June 25, 2009) was an American actress.

Marlon Brando: Marlon Brando Jr. (April 3, 1924 – July 1, 2004) was an American actor.

Unforgiven is a 1992 American revisionist Western film produced and directed by Clint Eastwood from a screenplay by David Webb Peoples.
In what year was Knights of the Zodiac first released?
